title: ProbeResult
description: v2 (2026-07-29): outcome of one dry-run request through an agent's current chain — 「试跑一次」 in the agent drawer footer (spec §10.1). Answers 'is this actually working right now' without making the user start a real turn, and replaces the session-level source pinning we explicitly do not build (spec §9). Inherits the resolution-event redaction invariant: classified outcomes only, never raw upstream error bodies. NOTE the outcome field is `reachable`, not `ok`: this object is nested under the standard envelope (`{ok: true, probe: ProbeResult}`), where `ok` already means 'the API call itself succeeded'. A probe that cleanly establishes the upstream is broken is a successful API call reporting `reachable: false` — the two must not share a name.

reachable.description: Whether the probed source actually answered. Never conflate with the envelope's `ok`.

source_id.description: The source that served (or failed) the probe — the first runnable candidate in this backend's chain for the probed model. Null is reserved for defensive serialization only: a probe with no runnable candidate fails with probe_no_candidate instead of returning this object.

model_id.description: The model actually sent upstream, mapping applied (the resolved id, not the menu identifier the caller passed in).

latency_ms.description: Round trip of the minimal request. null when the attempt never completed (network failure, timeout) — the UI must render that as 未完成, never as 0 ms.

error.description: i18n key when reachable=false, reusing the source detail_key vocabulary (models.source.cooldown.*, models.source.needs_action.*). Never raw upstream text. Explicitly null when reachable=true — the key is always present, so clients never have to distinguish absent from null.

via_mapping.description: true when a per-agent mapping rewrote the requested model id for this probe. null only when no candidate was resolved.
